answer_1.quote: We demonstrate that MUC effectively reduces confident hallucinations, achieving an average relative reduction of 29.6% in short-form QA tasks.
answer_1.outputs: Model-generated answers to questions, including nuanced uncertainty expressions (e.g., 'Hmm, maybe Bournemouth?')

answer_2.quote: Evaluation Metrics To evaluate the hallucination level and the calibration of verbal and semantic uncertainties, we use the following metrics: • Overall Hallucination Rate... • Confident Hallucination Rate... • Correctness Rate...

answer_3.quote: We follow recent work in expression decisiveness quantification and employ 'LLM-as-a-Judge' to measure VU.

answer_4.quote: We conduct a human evaluation on the judgment of verbal uncertainty... 4 authors of this paper then manually annotated an integer decisiveness score on a scale of 1 to 5
answer_4.guideline: Annotators assigned scores based on hedging expressions in answers using examples like 'I'm not really sure about this'
